Calculator.title: DTR Calculator
Calculator.intro: See how a game or a whole matchday changes the DTR. Pick real players to fill in their DTR and K exactly, or type the numbers yourself.
Calculator.newcomerLabel: Fewer than 30 rated games so far (+4)

Calculator.enterNumbers: Enter a DTR for every player to see the result.
Calculator.formulaChange: Change = (result − win chance) × K, rounded — result is 1 for a win, 0 for a loss.
Calculator.startOfDayNote: Every game of a matchday is calculated with the ratings from the start of the day; the changes are added up at the end.
Calculator.tableIntro: How many points you gain for a win or lose for a loss, depending on how much stronger or weaker your opponent is. Only the gap counts, not how high your DTR is. Each row starts where the points change.
Calculator.tableExample: Example with K = 16: you have 1500, your opponent 1560 (gap +60). A win gets you +11, a loss costs you −5.

HomePage.title: FLTT DTR Ranking
HomePage.intro1: DTR (Dëschtennis-Rating) is a rating that tracks every player's real playing strength, recalculated after each match of the {season} season. It's based on the same system used for the German TTR rating: win a match against a similarly-rated opponent and your rating goes up by a handful of points; lose, and it goes down. Beating a much stronger player is worth more, losing to a much weaker one costs more.
HomePage.intro2: Every player started the season with a baseline rating: adult players began at 1025, Juniors at 950, and younger players began lower still (900 or 850, depending on age group) since the rating hasn't yet had a chance to reflect their real strength. From there, every match this season has moved each player's rating up or down to where it stands today.

AboutPage.title: About this site
AboutPage.intro: This site tracks a DTR (Dëschtennis-Rating) for every player in the FLTT Verbandsrangliste — a rating that starts from a baseline value and moves up or down after every match of the season, the same way the German TTR rating works.
AboutPage.dataSourceBody: Match histories are taken from the FLTT match exports and run through the DTR formula (see DëschTennisRating.pdf) to produce a per-match DTR change for every player. Calculations start with the 2025-2026 season's data, and the site keeps updating and running with the latest results to stay current.
AboutPage.startingValuesBody: Every player begins the season at a baseline rating rather than an estimate carried over from elsewhere: adult players start at 1025, Juniors at 950, and younger youth players lower still depending on their age group (900 for Cadets/Minimes, 850 for Benjamins/Poussins), since a new player hasn't yet built up match results that reflect their real strength.
AboutPage.startingValuesHistoricalNote: These baseline values were originally cross-checked against an older estimate this site used before the DTR season simulation existed: a German TTR rating derived directly from each player's FLTT PFW score and class, using a regression fitted to 41 players who appeared in both rankings (PFW ≈ 0.596 × TTR − 588, R² = 0.78). That PFW-based estimate is no longer shown — DTR, calculated from real matches, replaced it — but it's kept here for reference.
AboutPage.kFactorBody: K determines how many points a single win or loss moves a player's DTR — a higher K means bigger swings, useful while a rating is still settling. The base is 16. Youth players get an age bonus on top: +8 for Poussins, Benjamins, Minimes and Cadets (under 15), or +4 for Juniors and Espoirs (under 21) — only one age bonus ever applies, they don't stack across brackets. Anyone with fewer than 30 matches in their career gets an extra +4 while their rating is still new, and a player returning after 12+ months away gets +4 back for their next 15 matches. These bonuses add on top of the base — see "Why this K?" on any player's profile for their exact current breakdown.
AboutPage.inactivityBody: A player who goes 24 months or more without a rated match starts losing DTR points, since a rating that hasn't been tested in that long no longer reflects their real current strength: −80 points at 24 months, a further −20 at 30 months, and a final −20 at 36 months, for a maximum deduction of −120. Youth players are exempt from this rule.
AboutPage.distributionSubtitle: How today's {count, number} DTR values are spread out, grouped into bands of 100 points.
AboutPage.lineupRulesIntro2: splits a club's checked-off players into teams of 4, ranked strongest to weakest by DTR — normally a player can't be listed ahead of anyone with a meaningfully higher DTR, since that would misrepresent the playing order. But small gaps are allowed, so two players close in strength can still be swapped without that counting as out of order. The limit is the same within one team and between a club's teams; it only loosens when either player involved is a youth player.
AboutPage.tableYouth: Either player is a youth player
AboutPage.lineupRulesFootnote: The rule is checked between every pair of players in the lineup, not just neighbors: a chain of small swaps can otherwise add up to two players ending up further apart than the limit allows, even though each individual swap looked fine.
AboutPage.lineupRulesAdjacentOnly: In Championnat Seniors, teams playing in NL1–NL3 follow a stricter rule instead: a player there can only swap with the spot directly above or below them — including across two of the club's NL teams — no matter how far apart their DTRs are. NL teams line up by the Verbandsrangliste — every player's DTR frozen on 1 August and again on 1 January — rather than by today's DTR, and nobody can end up more than one spot away from their place on it. The club's teams below NL3 keep the limits in the table above.
